Tungsten pressure calibrant; the static-DAC Dewaele et al. (2004) Vinet fit is the default, with Cu-referenced Shen and Smith and Sokolova et al. fits as alternatives. The legacy Hixson-Fritz BM3 record was removed because the cited shock paper publishes Hugoniot-derived tabular isotherms, not the migrated standalone BM3 reduction.

## Automatic selections

- **Equilibrium:** [tungsten\_dewaele\_2004\_vinet\_2](#record-tungsten_dewaele_2004_vinet_2)
- **Hugoniot:** None

The calculation cannot recover the eleven EOS parameter sets independently because the source omits complete thermochemical/ultrasonic rows, weights, and covariance.

This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The \*\_sokolova\_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source\_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

(1986) reduction (A=1904 GPa, B=7.665); P'\_R is the Dewaele et al. revision (A=1904 GPa, B=9.5). The paper states a common 0.01 angstrom^3/atom volume uncertainty and a pressure uncertainty increasing from 0.05 GPa at 1 GPa to 2 GPa at 150 GPa, but prints neither row-wise pressure errors nor raw R1 wavelengths.

### shen\_smith\_2026\_table\_s1\_simultaneous\_volumes

- **Description:** All 3,511 non-missing unit-cell volume measurements and standard errors from the two Supplemental Table S1 worksheets.
- **Kind:** simultaneous\_unit\_cell\_volumes
- **Reference:**
    - **Authors:** Shen; Smith
    - **Year:** 2026
    - **Source:** Phys. Rev. B
    - **Volume:** 113
    - **Locator:** 144113
    - **DOI:** 10.1103/fxgq-96sg
- **Source location:** Supplemental Table S1 workbook, DAC-1 and DAC-2 worksheets
- **Associated EOS records:** tungsten\_shen\_2026\_vinet\_3
- **Notes:** The source workbook contains 228 numbered DAC-1 runs and 194 numbered DAC-2 runs. Each non-missing volume/error pair was normalized to one CSV row while retaining the experiment and run identifiers; blank and '--' cells were omitted, not inferred. Pt measurements bracketing each scan retain their source first/last sequence labels. Phase labels distinguish bcc-Fe from hcp-Fe and NaCl-B1 from NaCl-B2. The workbook defines the errors as standard errors combining peak-fitting standard deviations and dispersion among volumes from different (hkl) peaks. Cu reference volumes are included even though no separate Shen-Smith Cu EOS record is bundled. The complete workbook is retained rather than only the lower-scatter run subsets used for the preferred fits.
